newsitem.title: UK: New UK govt turns down public inquiry into Lloyd's.
newsitem.headline: New UK govt turns down public inquiry into Lloyd's.

text.p: The new Labour government on Thursday endorsed the decision of the previous Conservative administration not to hold an independent judicial inquiry into the financial affairs of the Lloyd's of London insurance market.

Junior trade and industry minister Barbara Roche said the market's losses had already been thoroughly investigated in some 27 independent reviews as well as in probes by the Department of Trade and Industry and the Serious Fraud Office.

Moreover, an investigation would have to be carried out under the Tribunals of Enquiry Act of 1921, which would be extremely costly and could take years to complete, Roche said in a written parliamentary answer.
The government is considering future regulatory arrangements for Lloyd's but does not believe a further inquiry into past events would materially help it make up its mind, she added.
"Under the circumstances, I do not, therefore, propose to establish a public inquiry," Roche said.
